classes.name: Doorashada Madaxweynaha iyo Madaxweyne-ku-xigeenka
classes.finest_note: Votes by district and region in the Commission's 2010 declaration; by polling station (1,642) in 2017.
classes.locator: https://somalilandparliament.net/storage/uploads/settings/1772431097Constitution.pdf (Qodobka 83aad: direct, secret election of the President and Vice-President on one ticket; Qodobka 88aad: five-year term, two terms at most)
classes.note: The ticket with the most valid votes wins; there is no runoff. Before the 2001 Constitution, Presidents were chosen by the community conferences of Burao (1991), Borama (1993), and Hargeisa (1997) (see the class shir_beeleed). Vice-President Dahir Riyale Kahin succeeded on President Egal's death in May 2002 without an election. Polls fell due in 2008 and 2022 but were held in 2010 and 2024 after the House of Elders extended the incumbents' terms.

classes.name: Doorashada Golaha Wakiilada
classes.finest_note: Party and candidate votes by region.
classes.locator: https://somalilandparliament.net/storage/uploads/settings/1772431097Constitution.pdf (Qodobka 40aad: 82 members by direct, secret election; Qodobka 42aad: five-year term)
classes.note: The 82 members are elected in six regional constituencies (Hargeisa or Marodijeh 20, Togdheer 15, Awdal 13, Sanaag 12, Sool 12, Sahil 10) by list PR with largest remainders, the seats going to each party's candidates in order of their personal votes (Law 20-2/2005 art. 12; Law 91/2020 art. 77). A vacancy goes to the next reserve candidate on the party's list, so there are no by-elections (Law 91/2020 art. 78). From 1993 to 2005 the House was chosen by the clan conferences; the House elected in 2005 sat, by repeated extensions, until 2021.

classes.name: Doorashada Golayaasha Deegaanka (dawladaha hoose)
classes.finest_note: Party and association votes by region in the Commission's 2012 summary; district results are not online.
classes.locator: http://www.somalilandlaw.com/General_Law_National_Elections___Voter_Registration_No_91-2020_Unofficial-translation.pdf (art. 10(3): five-year term; arts. 79-80: open-list PR by district, council sizes by the Regions and Districts Law)
classes.note: Each district elects its council by party or association lists; the council then elects the mayor and deputy mayor. In 2002 the 23 districts were graded, with 25 councillors in Hargeisa and 21, 17, 13, or 9 elsewhere by grade. The nation-wide council votes of 2002 and 2012 also decided which three associations became the national parties (Political Parties and Associations Law art. 6).

classes.name: Doorashada Ururada Siyaasadda
classes.name_en: Contest of political associations for national party status
classes.note: The Constitution allows three national parties (art. 9). Registered political associations and the sitting parties contest a nation-wide vote every ten years, and the three with the most support across the regions become the national parties. In 2002 and 2012 that vote was the district council election itself, counted in golaha_deegaanka; in 2024 it was a separate ballot held with the presidential election.

dates.note: Held with the presidential election; the Commission's results were not reachable from here.

classes.name: Golaha Guurtida
classes.disposition_reason: The 82 Elders were chosen by their communities at the Borama (1993) and Hargeisa (February 1997) conferences, vacancies are filled by the clans, and the House has extended its own term since 2003; the Constitution leaves the method to a law (art. 58), and the only bill for direct elections was rejected by the Elders on 23 September 2006. No public vote has been held.

classes.name: Shirarka beelaha (1991-1997)
classes.name_en: Community conferences that chose the President and Parliament, 1991-1997
classes.disposition_reason: The Burao conference of May 1991, the Borama conference of 1993, and the Hargeisa conference of 1996-1997 chose the President and the members of both Houses by delegates of the clans, not by any public vote, and published no returns.

classes.name: Doorashada Duqa Magaalada
classes.disposition_reason: Mayors are elected by the district councillors from among themselves, not by the voters.

classes.name: Golayaasha Gobollada
classes.disposition_reason: The Constitution provides for regional councils (art. 111), but the election laws of 2001 and 2020 elect only district councils, and no regional council has been elected.

classes.name: Garsoorka
classes.disposition_reason: The President appoints the Chief Justice and the Supreme Court judges after consulting the Judicial Commission, and the two Houses confirm the Chief Justice (Constitution art. 105); no judicial office is elected.

classes.name: Xulashada musharaxiinta xisbiyada
classes.disposition_reason: Parties choose their presidential tickets and their candidate lists under their own rules and hand them to the Commission; the state runs and publishes no primaries.
